summary: Beaver Hill (Coos Co., OR): 50-ft tower built 1934, 40-ft live-in tower 1958, both lost in the 1962 Columbus Day storm; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in the Columbus Day storm of 1962; no source read describes the site today

staffing.status: staffed in 1934 (Charles Freeland named as lookout in a Coos Bay Times item); later staffing not in the sources read

access.note: No source read says whether the site is open to the public

facts.agency: Coos FPA (Former Fire Lookout Sites); Coos County Fire Patrol (Forest Lookouts)

events.note: Road work under way by November 1933 (Samuel L. Miller field report); The Forest Log item in December 1933 called it the Beaver Hill Lookout
50-foot wooden tower built on the site; L-4 cab, built by men from the Coquille CCC camp
Charles Freeland named as lookout at the Beaver Hill station (Coos Bay Times item, July 1934)
AWS cabin added to the site
40-foot wooden live-in tower built to replace the 1934 tower and cabin (register, firelookout.com); the 1958 district report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives the replacement towers as 50 feet
1958 tower destroyed in the Columbus Day storm
Registered November 22, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites names Coos FPA; Forest Lookouts names the Coos County Fire Patrol, and a 1934 Coos Bay Times item names the Coos Fire Patrol. The sources appear to describe the same patrol, so the register name is kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: gone, Coos FPA, 2010-era registration and 607 ft all match. Brief height 15.2 m (50 ft) is the 1934 tower only; the 1958 replacement was 40 ft (about 12.2 m) per the register and firelookout.com, but the 1958 district report quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 50 ft, so the record should say which tower the height describes. Brief design 'L-4' is supported only for the 1934 tower. Access 'unknown' is kept from the record: no source read says whether the site is public. The Forest Lookouts page now reads in full, so its 1936 fire entry (a lookout beat back flames threatening his tower) is complete; it is not used in the story. Do not use Wikipedia's 'Beaver Hill, Oregon' for the lookout: that article is a coal-mining ghost town whose coordinates are a few kilometres from the lookout's, and it says only that nothing is left of the town. The register's photo (courtesy Howard Verschoor) has no image URL in our data, so no photo is recorded. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story states the 40 ft versus 50 ft disagreement about the 1958 replacement without choosing one; the sources read do not settle it.
